renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Always fully awake, he sees himself by himself — nothing else is left. Being always awake wears the mind away, and from that wearing comes true seeing. Turned back into self-awareness with no twoness, he is king of yogis, a sun against the dark of not-knowing.

The moon is dimmed by the joy of tasting your own nature; with the inner sense gone, what is left to get? Self-knowledge and rest, firm and bright — freed from the whirl, aloneness comes soon. For yogis grounded in themselves, release is easy.

I have won rest in my own form, my sorrows are over, the split of grasped and grasper is broken — I stand firm as I am. Risen or gathered in, whoever wins that taste knows what is real. His stand never slips, so scripture-quarrels do nothing to him. Freed from delusion, living among people with no fear — free while alive.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Permanently awake, seeing self by self — zero remainder. Staying awake dissolves the mind; from that dissolve, true seeing. Turned inward with no twoness — king of yogis, sun against the dark of cluelessness.

Moon looks dim next to tasting your own nature; inner organ gone, nothing left to get. Self-knowledge plus rest, locked and lit — whirlings dropped, aloneness loading soon. Grounded yogis get release on easy mode.

Rest in my form: secured. Sorrows: done. Grasper-grasped split: broken. I stand firm as I am. Up or inward — whoever bags that taste knows the Real. His stand never slips; scripture-beef does nothing. Delusion shed, living with people, zero fear — free while alive.
